universes.name: Room 33
universes.description: A fantasy-meets-reality universe layered on Vashon Island's real history. At the heart of the island stands a lodge that has existed in various forms since time immemorial — first as a S'Homamish gathering place, then a pioneer inn, then a resort, now a weathered retreat. Room 33 is the nexus: a place where the boundaries between eras weaken and the island's deep memory surfaces. Writers, seekers, and the simply lost are drawn here, discovering they can step between time periods at certain thin points — the shell midden at Burton Acres, the old-growth ravines, the abandoned Nike missile base. But the past cannot be changed, only witnessed. And the island has its own will.
universes.logline: A bartender at a remote Pacific Northwest lodge discovers she may have been serving drinks — and writing the same unfinished novel — across multiple decades, guided by a room that exists outside of time.
universes.primeDirective: Every story element must serve emotional truth over plot mechanics. The lodge is a mirror, not a maze.

seasonArcs.title: The Threshold
seasonArcs.centralQuestion: What happens when you stop running?

seasonArcs.title: The Storm
seasonArcs.centralQuestion: What are you willing to lose?

worldRules.title: The Lodge Chooses
worldRules.description: The lodge selects its guests through forces beyond coincidence or intent.
worldRules.expanded: Every guest, every worker, every soul who crosses the threshold was summoned by forces older than memory. The lodge is not a trap — it is an invitation.

worldRules.title: Time Is Not Linear Here
worldRules.description: Temporal boundaries inside and around the lodge are fluid and permeable.
worldRules.expanded: A guest may hear music from 1935 in a 2024 hallway. A storm in the present may reveal the lodge as it was in 1910. Time is the lodge's native language.

worldRules.title: The Storm Is a Character
worldRules.description: Storms are not weather events but narrative forces that respond to emotional states.
worldRules.expanded: Each storm strips away a layer of pretense. The bigger the lie a guest carries, the fiercer the storm that greets them.

worldRules.title: Mixie Remembers Everything
worldRules.description: The bartender has served across all eras and retains memory of every guest and event.
worldRules.expanded: Mixie has served every era, every guest. She does not age. She does not forget. She does not judge. But she remembers.

worldRules.title: No One Leaves Until They're Ready
worldRules.description: The lodge holds guests for exactly as long as they need, no more, no less.
worldRules.expanded: Some guests stay a night. Some stay decades. The lodge does not imprison — it holds, teaches, and waits.

worldRules.title: The Lodge Is Not Evil
worldRules.description: The lodge reflects truth, which can feel painful but is never malicious.
worldRules.expanded: The lodge is a mirror, not a monster. What feels like cruelty is clarity. What feels like a cage is a chrysalis.

worldRules.title: Every Object Has Memory
worldRules.description: Physical objects within the lodge retain emotional impressions from those who have touched them.
worldRules.expanded: A glass left on the bar holds the sorrow of the hand that set it down. A key remembers every lock it has opened. Objects are witnesses.

worldRules.title: Music Is a Portal
worldRules.description: Music can transport guests across time and identity within the lodge.
worldRules.expanded: The right melody at the right moment can pull a guest into a different time, a different version of themselves. The jukebox is not random.

worldRules.title: Room 33 Is the Heart
worldRules.description: Room 33 is the lodge's core — a space that manifests differently for every guest.
worldRules.expanded: What happens inside Room 33 is different for every guest. Some emerge transformed. Some emerge terrified. Some do not emerge at all — at least not in the same era they entered.

worldRules.title: Confession Is Currency
worldRules.description: Honesty is rewarded with insight; deception triggers escalation.
worldRules.expanded: The lodge rewards honesty with revelation and punishes deception with escalation. A lie told at the bar may summon a storm.

worldRules.title: The Forest Watches
worldRules.description: The surrounding forest is an extension of the lodge's awareness and will.
worldRules.expanded: Trees that have stood for centuries serve as the lodge's perimeter, its early warning system, its dreamscape. Lost guests find themselves among roots that seem to guide — or mislead.

worldRules.title: Names Have Power
worldRules.description: Naming a fear or truth gives a guest power over it within the lodge.
worldRules.expanded: Guests who can name their fear begin to master it. The lodge asks each soul: what do you call the thing you carry?

worldRules.title: The Fourth Wall Is Thin
worldRules.description: The boundary between the story world and the audience is occasionally breached.
worldRules.expanded: Occasional moments of uncanny awareness — a glance at the camera, a line that speaks directly to the viewer — remind us that the lodge exists between worlds, including the one where we sit watching.

worldRules.title: Every Exit Is Also an Entrance
worldRules.description: Leaving the lodge is itself a transformation; the outside world is seen with new eyes.
worldRules.expanded: Guests who leave are changed. The world they return to has not changed — but they see it differently. Some find they cannot stop hearing the lodge's music.

worldRules.title: The Story Serves the Feeling
worldRules.description: Emotional resonance takes priority over plot cleverness in all narrative decisions.
worldRules.expanded: If a plot point is clever but emotionally hollow, it is cut. If a moment is simple but devastating, it stays. The story bows to the heart.

episodes.title: Pressure in the Air
episodes.theme: What happens when something is about to change?

episodes.title: Regulars
episodes.theme: What patterns do we build to avoid change?
episodes.coldOpen: 1935, M. Quinn tends bar looking like Mixie.

episodes.title: The Woman in the Storm
episodes.theme: What stories do we tell about the things we cannot explain?
episodes.majorEvent: Major storm. Time slip shows 1935 bar.

episodes.title: Room 33
episodes.theme: What happens when you stop resisting?

episodes.title: Static
episodes.theme: What happens when reality contradicts itself?

episodes.title: The Photograph
episodes.theme: What if you are not who you think you are?
episodes.majorEvent: Mixie finds M. Quinn in ledger, handwriting matches. She writes letter to Room 33, gets skeleton key back.

episodes.title: What the Storm Took
episodes.theme: What is the cost of knowing?
episodes.majorEvent: Sam and Mixie discover Room 33/disappearance correlation. Mixie realizes novel is transcription.

episodes.title: The Foresters
episodes.theme: What happens when people try to own what should be tended?
episodes.majorEvent: Foresters revealed. 'Callahan' in ledger. 1943 unfinished letter.

episodes.title: The Other Draft
episodes.theme: What happens when the author enters the story?
episodes.majorEvent: Three earlier novel drafts found. Mixie enters Room 33. Encounters Siobhan in mirror. Dies. Flynn's vigil. Tom's speech.

episodes.title: Check-Out Time
episodes.theme: What does it mean to stop running from who you are?
episodes.majorEvent: Rebirth. Novel finished. Jauncey's original song. New guest arrives. Distant thunder.

items.name: The Photograph
items.significance: Central mystery object linking Mixie to M. Quinn across decades.
items.description: A framed photograph behind the bar of a woman who looks exactly like Mixie, dated to the mid-twentieth century. Its presence is the first crack in Mixie's understanding of herself.

items.name: Guest Ledger
items.significance: Historical record containing M. Quinn entries and Forester connections.
items.description: A leather-bound guest register that has recorded every arrival since the lodge opened in 1910. Contains M. Quinn entries with handwriting that matches Mixie's own.

items.name: Mixie's Notebook
items.significance: The novel Mixie is writing, which may be a transcription rather than an original work.
items.description: A handwritten novel-in-progress that Mixie believes she is composing. Earlier drafts from 1936, 1938, and 1942 are discovered, suggesting the novel writes itself through whoever tends bar.

items.name: The Piano
items.significance: Instrument that plays autonomously during storms, bridging eras through music.
items.description: An upright piano in the Triangle Bar that plays untouched during storms. Its melodies correspond to songs from different decades, as if the lodge is cycling through its own memory.

items.name: The Mirror
items.significance: Portal and truth-teller; Siobhan's primary connection point across time.
items.description: An antique mirror that reflects a fraction of a second late. Connected to Siobhan's legend and Room 33. Functions as a portal between eras for those the lodge has chosen.

items.name: Room 33 Key
items.significance: The lodge's response to Mixie's letter — an invitation to the heart.
items.description: A brass skeleton key returned by Room 33 after Mixie writes a letter and slides it under the door. The key did not exist before this moment; it was created by the room in response to honest confession.

items.name: Flynn's Pocket Watch
items.significance: Temporal anomaly object that responds to the lodge's shifts in time.
items.description: A pocket watch carried by Flynn, composed of parts that self-assemble during storms. When the lodge shifts between eras, the watch disassembles and reassembles to show a different time.

items.name: The Sea That Held Her
items.significance: Original song that serves as the emotional climax of Season 1.
items.description: An original song composed and performed by Jauncey in the season finale. The song channels everything the lodge has taught its guests about holding on and letting go.

items.name: Foresters' Symbols
items.significance: Evidence of a secret society's long involvement with the lodge.
items.description: Compass roses and coded marks carved, painted, and embedded throughout the lodge by the Foresters, a secret society that has attempted to study and control the lodge's power for over a century.

items.name: Brass Bell
items.description: A service bell at the front desk that rings on its own during storms. Its tone changes depending on the severity of the approaching temporal disturbance.

items.name: Tom's Tools
items.significance: Collection of anomalous objects recovered from the lodge's fireplace.
items.description: A workshop and cigar box containing 37 objects pulled from the fireplace ash over the years. Each object belongs to a different era. Tom catalogues them without fully understanding their origin.

items.name: Foresters' Journal
items.significance: Secret society records revealing the lodge's deeper history and the Callahan connection.
items.description: Records from a locked cabinet containing the Foresters' membership ledger. The name 'Callahan' appears, connecting the secret society to the lodge's founding and its supernatural properties.

items.name: Abandoned Belongings
items.significance: Physical evidence of guests who entered Room 33 and never returned to their own time.
items.description: Personal items left behind by guests who vanished from the lodge. The most notable is the Voss steamer trunk, packed as if for departure but never collected.

items.name: Unlabeled Bottle
items.significance: Subtle supernatural presence behind the bar — the lodge's quiet persistence.
items.description: A mystery bottle kept behind the bar whose liquid level never changes regardless of how much is poured. No one remembers when it arrived or what it contains.

items.name: Library Clock
items.significance: Temporal barometer connected to the lodge's mechanical heart.
items.description: A grandfather clock in the library that is mechanically synced with the boiler. During storms, both accelerate together, as if the lodge's heartbeat quickens in anticipation.

items.name: Landscape Painting
items.significance: Visual evidence that the lodge reshapes its own interior according to its mood.
items.description: A painting hung above the fireplace that changes subtly between viewings. Guests who look closely notice different seasons, different figures in the distance, different light.

items.name: Amber's Photograph
items.significance: Season Two mystery seed planted in Season One.
items.description: A photo album containing images shot from impossible angles — inside walls, beneath floors, from the perspective of the lodge itself. Intended as the entry point for Season Two's central mystery.
